title: Backpropagation on a tape
starter:
type node = X of float | Const of float | Add of int * int | Mul of int * int

(* d(last entry)/d(entry i) for every i. Add and Mul index earlier entries. *)
let grads (tape : node list) : float list =
  let n = List.length tape in
  List.init n (fun i -> if i = n - 1 then 1.0 else 0.0)   (* only the seed so far *)
hints: Two passes. Forward: compute each entry's value in order into an array. Backward: from the last entry down to the first.
An `Add` passes its gradient to both operands unchanged. A `Mul` passes `g *. (the other operand's value)` to each side.
Accumulate with `g.(a) <- g.(a) +. ...`: an entry used twice (like `Mul (0, 0)`) receives two contributions, and the derivative is their sum.
explain: This is reverse mode in miniature. Walking the tape backward guarantees every entry has received all its contributions before it passes its own gradient on, because users always come later on the tape than what they use. `x *. x` at 3 gives 6: two contributions of 3 each. Accumulating is the whole trick, and it's why the spec has to say in which order the contributions are added: in f32, the order changes the bits.
